daniel_intro.014: The blue whale with the faded smile.

daniel_intro.016: The green dinosaur missing one felt tooth.
daniel_intro.017: The dinosaur! Missing a tooth. That's not a flaw, that's a personality.

daniel_intro.019: The star. Upside down. In the worst corner. You have taste *and* no mercy.
daniel_intro.020: He feeds in a coin. Charlie drums on the side of the cabinet. The claw descends with enormous confidence.
daniel_intro.021: It closes around your pick. It lifts it two centimetres. It thinks about it.

daniel_intro.033: Four chances to get it right. And if you don't, it's still funny. You can't lose in a photo booth.

daniel_route.083: It is just a room. The real one, behind door eight, the way it has been since the studio closed.
daniel_route.084: Bare floor. A radiator that ticks. One socket with a sticker on it that says DO NOT UNPLUG in three different people's handwriting.
daniel_route.085: The only light is a thin stripe under the door, from the hall.
daniel_route.086: Daniel is standing in the middle of it with his arms a little out from his sides, like someone who has just stepped off a boat.
daniel_route.091: He looks at you for a long second. Then at the floor. Then he sits — cross-legged, careful, the way you'd sit in a room where somebody is sleeping.
daniel_route.092: You sit down beside him. Backs against the wall. The radiator ticks.
daniel_route.096: His windbreaker rustles every time he breathes. He notices, and tries to breathe more quietly, which is somehow louder.
daniel_route.097: You don't laugh. It's very close.
daniel_route.099: Far below, someone in the lobby laughs, and a door closes, and the building settles around the sound like a cat.
daniel_route.101: You don't move. Neither does he. After a while, the not-moving becomes something you're doing together.
daniel_route.102: Let your shoulder rest against his.
daniel_route.103: His shoulder is tense for a second, like it's waiting for a joke to land. Then it isn't.
daniel_route.104: Turn your hand palm-up on the floor between you.
daniel_route.105: He looks at it for a long time.
daniel_route.108: His hand is warm, and a little sweaty from air hockey. He says so, very quietly, and apologises, and doesn't let go.
daniel_route.109: Can I say something? Not a bit. A real one.
daniel_route.111: I made the list because I thought—
daniel_route.112: If it went quiet, you'd notice there wasn't anything else. No arcade. No games. Just me, in a room.
daniel_route.113: And that's not— it's not much.
daniel_route.114: He says it to his knees. He says it without a single exclamation mark. You didn't know he owned a sentence like that.
daniel_route.115: "I came here for just you, in a room."
daniel_route.116: You can't just say that. In the dark. With no music.
daniel_route.117: I think this is the only place you can say it.
daniel_route.119: Oh, the radiator's carrying this whole scene.
daniel_route.120: It's a small laugh. A real one. It doesn't need anyone to hear it.
daniel_route.122: You stay. That's the whole answer. After a while he nods, like it was a good one.
daniel_route.123: Is this okay? This. Just this?
daniel_route.125: Can we do it a bit longer?
daniel_route.127: …What do you do? When it's quiet. Wherever you live now.
daniel_route.128: "Usually I leave before it gets quiet."
daniel_route.130: So this is new for you too.
daniel_route.132: Okay. Good. I mean— not good. Fair. It's fair.
daniel_route.135: It ticks. It's a good listener.
daniel_route.136: I'm going to be a good listener. Watch. Starting now.
daniel_route.141: He says it like a fact he's just checked, and found to be true.
daniel_route.143: I have one strip of film left in the reconstruction. Four frames. I would like to use it, if you would like to be in it.
daniel_route.145: Only the rain. It is in the record. I cannot take it out.
daniel_route.146: That's okay. The rain can stay.
daniel_route.147: The booth builds itself around the two of you out of soft light. The bench. The curtain. The little screen.
daniel_route.148: The rain on the roof. The same rain, applauding nobody.
daniel_route.149: This time nobody has to run. You're already sitting down. Mr. Kim's former prisoner sits in your lap, facing the lens.
daniel_route.150: The screen lights up. FOUR FRAMES. SMILE!
daniel_route.151: Oh no. It's going. Okay, okay, pose—
daniel_route.152: FRAME ONE. His hand comes up — peace sign, tongue half out — and stops halfway, like he's just remembered he doesn't have to.
daniel_route.153: He laughs at himself, and puts the hand down.
daniel_route.154: Pull a face at the camera.
daniel_route.155: FRAME TWO. You, making the worst face of your life on purpose. Daniel, staring at you, delighted and betrayed. That was supposed to be his job.
daniel_route.156: Look at him instead of the camera.
daniel_route.157: FRAME TWO. The camera catches you looking at him. It catches him catching you. Neither of you looks away in time.
daniel_route.158: Sit still and let it happen.
daniel_route.159: FRAME TWO. Two people on a bench. One of them is trying very hard not to grin, and losing.
daniel_route.160: FRAME THREE. Both of you laughing at nothing in particular, which is the best thing there is to laugh at.
daniel_route.161: The screen counts down to the last frame. Five. Four.
daniel_route.164: He turns towards you. Slowly, so you can see it coming. So you could say no.
daniel_route.167: He leans in until his forehead rests against yours. His hair is soft and ridiculous and smells faintly of the arcade.
daniel_route.168: Your hand is still in his. It has been, the whole time.
daniel_route.169: He finds your hand without looking, and asks with his thumb, and you answer the same way.
daniel_route.171: He leans back against the booth wall. After a second, his shoulder settles against yours, and stays.
daniel_route.172: He doesn't look at the camera. He looks at the curtain, and the rain, and — once, quickly, like he's checking you're still there — at you.
daniel_route.175: Nobody posing. Nobody performing. Two people on a bench, waiting out a rain that is only a memory, in no hurry at all for it to stop.
daniel_route.176: The booth prints the strip with a whirr and a small, satisfied click.
daniel_route.177: RECORD 08. FRAMES FIVE THROUGH EIGHT: APPENDED. CONDITION: DRY.
daniel_route.178: I have never added to a record before. I believe it was allowed.
daniel_route.179: Daniel holds the new strip up by one corner, like it might still be wet.
daniel_route.180: Frame one: me, quitting halfway. That's growth. Write that down.
daniel_route.181: Frame three: we look insane. Good. Correct.
daniel_route.182: And look at the last one.
daniel_route.183: That's my favourite. Again. Two for two.
daniel_route.184: The booth dims around you until it is only the room again. The radiator. The stripe of light under the door.
daniel_route.186: Hey. Do you want to know what number eleven was? On the list?
daniel_route.188: "Sit somewhere with {{playerName}}." I put it last. I didn't think we'd get to it.
daniel_route.189: We got to it early. Kind of. I skipped five whole things.
daniel_route.190: Songha's going to look at this page and think I got kidnapped.
daniel_route.191: Tell him number eleven took longer than planned.
daniel_route.193: I don't want to plan anything else tonight. I just want—
daniel_route.194: Can I just want this? Is that allowed?
daniel_route.196: He lets out a breath that sounds like it has been waiting two years.
daniel_route.197: I think I'm getting better at it. Nothing. Sitting.
daniel_route.199: Don't tell anyone. I have a reputation.
daniel_route.200: All recipients: please come to the lobby. It is almost time. I would like everyone to be there.
daniel_route.202: He stands, and pulls you up by the hand, and doesn't let go of it on the stairs. Not once.
daniel_route.203: He stands, and pulls you up by the hand, and lets go a second later than he needs to.
daniel_ending.001: The Archive Wall is almost dark now. Hundreds of little glass boxes, gone quiet one by one. Only the eighth is still lit.
daniel_ending.003: Writing four frames. Then four more. Then a note in the margin: "Condition: dry."
daniel_ending.004: A small glass card slides out of a slot in the front desk that you never knew was there. It is warm, like a cup someone has just put down.
daniel_ending.005: Inside the glass: eight tiny frames. A pose. A startle. Two strangers laughing. Two strangers sitting.
daniel_ending.006: Then the new four, all the way down to the last one, where nobody is doing anything at all.
daniel_ending.007: …It's so small. Why is it so small? I thought it'd be, like, a poster.
daniel_ending.008: Is that the booth one? Let me see— oh. *Oh*. Frame eight. Hyung.
daniel_ending.009: Of course it's the booth one. I would've put money on it. I did, actually. Hyunjun owes me three thousand won.
daniel_ending.010: I said the claw machine! That's basically the same thing! It's the same *genre*!
daniel_ending.011: Frame one's great, by the way. That's a professional pose. I respect it.
daniel_ending.012: The last frame is good. Nobody would have written it like that. That's why it works.
daniel_ending.015: Daniel doesn't say anything. He holds the card up to the last light of the Archive Wall and grins at it like it just told him a secret.
daniel_ending.016: Then he turns the card round so you can see it too, and keeps it there, between the two of you, where both of you can hold an edge.
daniel_ending.017: ECHO? Thanks. For keeping it. Even wet.
daniel_ending.018: You are welcome, Recipient Daniel. It was my favourite record to be bad at.
daniel_ending.019: Also, I'd like my notebook back.
daniel_ending.020: You'll get it back! I only used one page. And a half. There's a drawing of Mr. Kim.
daniel_ending.021: Hongdae at twenty to six is a different city. Shutters down. A street sweeper humming. Two pigeons holding a meeting about a dropped triangle kimbap.
daniel_ending.022: It's a fifteen-minute walk from Studio 25 to here. Daniel made it take forty.
daniel_ending.023: He stopped at every photo booth on the way and looked inside, like he was checking on old friends.
daniel_ending.024: The others went ahead to breakfast. Hamin said he'd order for everyone. Songha said he'd order for Hamin.
daniel_ending.025: The arcade is closed. The booth outside it is a newer one — pink, with a sticker promising the best photos in Mapo.
daniel_ending.026: The awning is exactly as useless as you remember.
daniel_ending.027: You and Daniel are sitting on the step beside it. Nobody decided to. It just happened, about twenty minutes ago.
daniel_ending.028: Mr. Kim's former prisoner sits on the step between you, watching the sky go from grey to peach.
daniel_ending.029: His phone buzzes. He reads it. He doesn't answer it.
daniel_ending.031: He stands, and stretches until something in his back clicks, and pats his pockets for nothing in particular.
daniel_ending.034: You said that twenty minutes ago.
daniel_ending.036: He looks at you. Then at the street. Then he sits back down.
daniel_ending.038: You have never once in your life asked for five more minutes.
daniel_ending.039: You were always the one who knew exactly when to leave. The thank-you over the shoulder. The curtain swinging shut behind you. The rain stopping, and you going with it.
daniel_ending.040: Daniel's head comes to rest on your shoulder, heavy and warm, and his hand finds yours on the step as if it has done it a hundred times.
daniel_ending.043: Okay. Just checking. I'm going to keep checking. Forever, probably.
daniel_ending.044: Daniel's shoulder settles against yours. His knee doesn't bounce once.
daniel_ending.047: I'm not going to say anything else. Look at me. Not saying anything else.
daniel_ending.048: He doesn't fill the silence. He doesn't need to.
daniel_ending.049: The street does it for him: a shutter going up, a bike bell, a pigeon with opinions. The light coming up over Mapo like it has nowhere else to be.
daniel_ending.052: Not the ECHO kind. The normal kind.
daniel_ending.053: This counts. This is my favourite frame.
daniel_ending.054: There's no camera. He doesn't seem to mind.
daniel_newmem.001: A week later. A Tuesday, which is the least eventful day ever invented.
daniel_newmem.002: Hongdae, three in the afternoon. The pink booth by the arcade has a queue of exactly one person, and he is waving at you with both arms.
daniel_newmem.003: {{playerName}}! You came! I wasn't sure you'd— no, I was sure. I was mostly sure.
daniel_newmem.004: Okay. So. ECHO's asleep. The Future Letter Project is closed. The studio is currently full of men with drills.
daniel_newmem.005: Which means somebody has to keep the archive going. Unofficially. Me. I'm the archive now.
daniel_newmem.007: One strip. Four frames. Every week, until I run out of money, which will be soon.
daniel_newmem.008: Songha made me a spreadsheet for it. Hanbi bought me a folder. Charlie keeps asking what the folder's for.
daniel_newmem.009: The booth is exactly as narrow as the other one. Some things are just standard.
daniel_newmem.010: Frame one, pose. Frame two, pose worse. Frame three, whatever happens happens.
daniel_newmem.014: Frame one: a peace sign, and a worse peace sign.
daniel_newmem.015: Frame two: a face you will deny making.
daniel_newmem.016: Frame three: whatever happened. It's mostly elbows.
daniel_newmem.017: Frame four: two people on a bench, not doing anything, for almost the whole three seconds.
daniel_newmem.018: Then, at the very last instant, Daniel's composure breaks, and the camera catches him laughing at absolutely nothing.
daniel_newmem.019: That still counts! Nobody said nothing had to be *quiet*.
daniel_newmem.020: The machine prints two copies, still warm. He hands you one without looking at it, like it was always going to be yours.
daniel_newmem.022: I was going to say that! That's my whole line. You keep taking my lines.
daniel_newmem.023: Tuck the strip into your coat. The inside pocket, where the rain can't get it.
daniel_newmem.024: …Good. Good pocket choice. Very dry. I approve.
daniel_newmem.026: Daniel looks at the sky, then at the booth, then at you.
